items.title: Noetra launches development of Japan’s multimodal AI foundation model for physical AI and robotics
items.summary: Noetra has initiated comprehensive research and development for a Japanese multimodal foundation model. This new model is designed to underpin advanced AI systems for both robotics and general physical artificial intelligence. The effort involves collaboration among Noetra's core members, including Sony, SoftBank, NEC, and Honda Motor. Furthermore, the development incorporates participation from numerous partners specializing in sovereign AI applications. Ultimately, the goal is to build a foundational AI layer specifically for advanced physical implementations of artificial intelligence within Japan.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Noetra launches development of Japan’s multimodal AI foundation model for physical AI and robotics." This report details the commencement of a major national initiative to develop a foundational artificial intelligence framework tailored for advanced robotic applications across Japan. The research effort involves core industry partners including Sony, SoftBank, NEC, and Honda Motor, alongside numerous specialists focusing on sovereign AI implementations. Through this collaborative methodology, the goal is the creation of an underlying AI layer specifically designed to support complex physical manifestations of artificial intelligence within Japanese infrastructure. This development signals a significant push toward integrating advanced multimodal processing directly into real-world physical automation systems nationwide.

items.title: Robbyant unveils LingBot-VLA 2.0 universal AI model for embodied robots
items.summary: Robbyant, an embodied AI company under Ant Group, has unveiled the upgraded and open-source LingBot-VLA 2.0. This next-generation model is a vision-language-action (VLA) architecture designed to serve as a universal brain for robots. Compared to its January 2026 predecessor, it demonstrates substantial improvements in several key areas. Specifically, the new version offers advanced morphological generalization capabilities. Furthermore, it supports increased degrees of freedom and boasts enhanced deployment efficiency.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Robbyant unveils LingBot-VLA 2.0 universal AI model for embodied robots." The report details the launch of an upgraded, open-source vision-language-action or VLA architecture intended to function as a comprehensive cognitive system for robotic platforms. This next-generation model exhibits notable advancements when benchmarked against its earlier iteration from January 2026. Key technical improvements include enhanced morphological generalization capabilities and expanded support for greater degrees of freedom, coupled with an increase in operational deployment efficiency. The availability of this sophisticated framework signals a significant development trajectory within the field of physical AI robotics research.

items.title: Brain implant helps paralysed man to feed himself and drink from cup
items.summary: A man previously paralyzed from the chest down following a swimming accident has regained significant function. Using a brain implant, which bypasses his spinal cord injury, Keith Thomas can now feed himself and drink from a cup. Initially unable to lift his arms, he underwent surgery to implant electrodes directly into his brain. Through subsequent months of rigorous training, he successfully regained the ability to move his limbs. This technology represents a significant breakthrough for individuals with severe spinal cord injuries.
items.audio_script: From The Guardian - Artificial Intelligence, "Brain implant helps paralysed man to feed himself and drink from cup". The story details how a paralyzed individual has regained significant function using a novel brain implant system. The subject, who suffered paralysis following a swimming accident, underwent surgery involving the implantation of electrodes directly into the brain. Subsequent months involved rigorous training protocols, leading to the successful regaining of limb movement capabilities. This technological advancement marks a notable breakthrough for individuals suffering from severe spinal cord injuries. Developments in neural interfaces suggest a pathway toward restoring motor function previously thought irreversible for many patients.

items.title: Has AI Agent Autonomy Redefined Robotics Safety and Control?
items.summary: Robotic systems are gaining the ability to perceive and change their behavior independently across various environments like warehouses and industries. While this autonomy enhances production and adaptability, it introduces complex issues regarding safety and control. To manage these risks, agent governance establishes guidelines for system capabilities, decision monitoring, and necessary human oversight. Safety measures are being developed, ranging from physical barriers to emergency protocols. Therefore, increased robot autonomy necessitates a refined framework for ensuring robust operational safety.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Has AI Agent Autonomy Redefined Robotics Safety and Control?". The report details how advancing autonomous robotic systems necessitate a complete overhaul of current safety protocols to manage enhanced operational capabilities. These sophisticated robots are demonstrating the ability to perceive environments and modify behavior independently across diverse settings such as industrial warehouses. To govern this increased capability, agent governance structures are being implemented, establishing formal guidelines for monitoring decision-making processes and defining necessary levels of human supervision alongside developing physical and procedural emergency safeguards. Consequently, the industry faces a requirement to integrate these evolving safety standards into every layer of robotic deployment architecture.

items.title: 🔬 The Lab of the Future Should Feel Like a Data Center — Andy Beam & Rafa Gómez-Bombarelli, Lila Sciences
items.summary: Lila Sciences envisions a "lab of the future" operating like an AI data center, utilizing automated robotics and equipment for continuous experimentation. Their ambitious goal is developing a scientific superintelligence wired directly into the wet lab environment. They aim to treat science as an infinite token generator by producing vast amounts of experimentally validated reasoning data across biology, chemistry, and materials science. This process involves building massive libraries of "scientific tokens" through high-throughput, iterative experimentation rather than solely focusing on raw volume. Ultimately, they seek a general model capable of solving diverse scientific problems through broad data generation.
items.audio_script: From Latent.Space, "🔬 The Lab of the Future Should Feel Like a Data Center — Andy Beam & Rafa Gómez-Bombarelli, Lila Sciences." This report outlines a concept for reimagining scientific research by integrating automated robotics and AI to create self-perpetuating experimental systems. Lila Sciences envisions treating science as an infinite data source by building a "scientific superintelligence" directly into the wet lab environment. The methodology involves conducting high-throughput, iterative experimentation across biology, chemistry, and materials science to generate libraries of validated reasoning data, termed scientific tokens. This approach shifts focus from merely generating large volumes of raw data to creating deeply structured, experimentally proven knowledge sets. These efforts point toward a future where general artificial models can solve diverse scientific problems through systematic, automated data generation.

items.title: How to Make an Invisible Drone
items.summary: Northwestern University roboticists demonstrated Phantom Twist, a drone designed for near-invisibility using computational design. The drone achieves its stealth by spinning rapidly (15 to 25 Hz), causing motion blur that leverages the human eye's "persistence of vision." This technique requires careful structural design so components align with empty space as it spins. The optimization process used a metric minimizing perceived image differences between background and drone overlays, achieving an LPIPS score far better than human-designed versions. While currently requiring an optical tracking system, future applications could include covert surveillance or 360-degree wildlife observation.
items.audio_script: From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "How to Make an Invisible Drone." The report details a system called Phantom Twist, which represents a breakthrough in stealth technology by designing a drone engineered for near-invisibility. Northwestern University roboticists achieved this effect by having the drone spin rapidly between fifteen and twenty-five cycles per second. This high-speed rotation generates motion blur that exploits the human eye's inherent persistence of vision. The structural design process involved optimizing components so they align precisely with empty background space while spinning, utilizing a metric that minimized perceived image differences. Currently necessitating an optical tracking system, future uses for this technology include covert surveillance applications and advanced 360-degree wildlife observation platforms.

items.title: Adaptive Control of Motor-Position-Controlled Flexible Joint Robots with Uncertain Joint Stiffness
items.summary: Model-based control of flexible joint robots using actuators that control position requires knowing the precise joint stiffness, which is often uncertain or changes over time due to wear. To address this, the paper proposes an adaptive control method to continuously estimate the unknown, nonlinear torque-deflection relationship at each joint. Unlike methods for non-elastic robots, this approach utilizes an implicit control law and a regressor matrix dependent on the control input. The proposed technique accounts for the uncertainties introduced by variable joint stiffness. Experimental validation on a flexible joint with non-linear stiffness confirms the effectiveness of this adaptive strategy.

items.title: Semantic Audio-driven Understanding for Dynamic Humanoid Whole Body Control
items.summary: Introduces a novel multi-modal framework for autonomous humanoid control driven by semantic audio input. The system processes continuous audio streams, splitting them into music and speech branches for specialized handling. Music input uses audio fingerprinting to map musical segments to appropriate motion policies. Speech input grounds direct human-robot interaction within a library of imitation-learned skills. This unified interface schedules skill execution through an RL control pipeline, demonstrating successful sim-to-real transfer on a physical humanoid robot.

items.title: Open-AoE: An Open Egocentric Manipulation Dataset and Toolchain for Embodied Learning
items.summary: Open-AoE is an open, community-oriented dataset and toolchain designed for embodied learning from egocentric manipulation videos. It features a first release of approximately 2,000 hours of footage collected by over 500 contributors using numerous smartphones. The resource provides rich annotations including text descriptions, MANO hand poses, camera trajectories, and atomic actions. A specialized data processing pipeline structures raw recordings through segmentation, semantic annotation, and reconstruction steps. Finally, an accompanying toolchain supports visualization, cross-embodiment retargeting, and training for various embodied AI policies.

items.title: Never Too Late for Force: Accelerating VLA Post-Training with Reactive Force Injection
items.summary: Pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies struggle in contact states due to limitations with visual input or minor errors. LIFT introduces a force-aware post-training framework by grafting a reactive action expert onto the existing VLA policy. This system injects real-time 6D end-effector force through a causal force memory and cross-attention mechanism for action refreshment during execution. To handle distribution shift from contact feedback, LIFT incorporates an online DAgger loop training on both offline data and human corrections. Experiments show LIFT surpasses vision-only methods in complex tasks like towel folding and book insertion, confirming the necessity of reactive force modeling.

items.title: MEMORA: Embodied Action Memory from Egocentric Videos for Reasoning and Planning
items.summary: Developing long-horizon robot planning requires embodied action memory beyond immediate scene prediction, incorporating past experiences like object changes and prior procedures. MEMORA implements this capability through a formation-consolidation-retrieval lifecycle utilizing four distinct memory stores: Environment, Entity, Activity, and Inferred Knowledge. Online editing updates memory with new observations while offline consolidation abstracts repeated actions into reusable patterns. Testing on EPIC-KITCHENS-100 data demonstrated that full MEMORA significantly improved both memory assessment accuracy (up to 20.5 points) and out-of-distribution planning scores (up to 16.6%). These results confirm that editable, consolidated memory effectively supplies remembered context for robust robot decision-making.

items.title: Stochastic Filtering for Quorum Sensing in Robot Swarms under Anonymous Communication
items.summary: Quorum Sensing (QS) is vital for robot swarm coordination, requiring individuals to accurately estimate the group quorum level through communication. Using anonymous protocols allows for scalability by exchanging local neighbor information without revealing identities. However, these anonymous methods can incorrectly double-count messages, biasing the overall quorum estimates. The study proposes a stochastic filtering protocol inspired by $k$-priority sampling ($\text{AN}^k$) to enhance estimate stability compared to baseline and randomized alternatives. $\text{AN}^k$ successfully stabilizes the estimate by actively filtering the message buffer, though it increases recovery time after errors.

items.title: DiMaS: Distribution Matching for Steering Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Flow-matching vision-language-action (VLA) models lack effective fine-grained behavioral control through internal representation manipulation. Existing linear steering techniques fail in the VLA setting because behavioral features are not linearly steerable, despite being linearly decodable. The paper introduces DiMaS, a Distribution-Matching Steering strategy designed specifically for flow-matching VLAs. DiMaS controls behavior by transporting between entire representation distributions rather than shifting along a fixed direction. Experiments demonstrate that this method effectively controls behavior in state-of-the-art VLAs and analyzes the generalizability of behavioral control across diverse tasks.

items.title: Beyond Visual Grasping: Benchmarking Complex Grasping from Detection to Execution
items.summary: Robust robotic grasping requires more than just visual grasp pose detection for real-world complexity. Existing benchmarks fail to test multi-step reasoning and semantic understanding during execution phases. Authors propose GCA-Bench, a new benchmark focusing on challenging "grasping with complex action" scenarios involving scene reasoning. Evaluating various baseline methods against this set revealed success rates below 70% in complex grasping tasks. The work also introduces new evaluation metrics to guide the development of more robust grasping strategies.

items.title: ConFlow: Constraints-Guided Learning with Flow Matching for Motion Generation
items.summary: Proposes ConFlow, a novel framework for generative robot motion modeling that addresses the limitations of current Flow Matching methods by integrating constraints directly into the training objective. It achieves this by employing differentiable barrier or cost functions to incorporate desired task-specific rules. Additionally, ConFlow replaces the standard Gaussian source distribution with a conditional Gaussian Process for improved specification adherence. The method utilizes infeasible demonstrations as negative supervision to enhance constraint satisfaction without extra expert data. Experiments on two-robot navigation show that ConFlow reduces collision rates and improves trajectory quality compared to standard flow matching baselines.
